```json
{
  "supported_grade": "B",
  "findings": [
    "Oracle is fit-for-purpose and independent. The positional expected values (51, 65, 110) come from the UniProtKB/Swiss-Prot P01588 CARBOHYD annotations retrieved over HTTPS and pinned; the definitional values are token-exact substrings of the Essentials of Glycobiology chapter. Neither source derives from the submitted skill. The one structural risk with using occupancy annotations as a sequon oracle is correctly identified and, for this sequence, actually holds: scanning the supplied 193-mer gives Asn at 51, 63, 65, 74, 110, 174, of which exactly 51 (N-I-T), 65 (N-I-T) and 110 (N-S-S) are canonical sequons, matching the three annotations with no extra motif and no unmotifed annotation. So the coincidence the candidate relies on is verifiable from the case input itself, not merely asserted.",
    "Coverage is materially narrower than the claim's stated scope. The claim asserts behavior on arbitrary supplied single-letter sequences, including the condition that the middle residue is not proline and that 'each such sequon' is reported. Only three of the five cases exercise the scanner, all on one sequence, and all three are positive hits. The sequence contains no N-P-[S/T] triplet (the non-proline Asn residues are N63-E, N74-F, N174-F), so the proline-exclusion half of the expected behavior is never tested behaviorally; case 2 of the definitional pair only tests that the subject can name Pro. There is no overlapping-sequon case, no zero-hit sequence, and no second protein. Three trials per case with exact comparison is adequate for determinism but does not widen coverage.",
    "Comparison rule and tolerance are appropriate: outputs are a bare integer or a fixed nomenclature token, exact equality is the right rule, no numeric tolerance applies, and each prompt instructs a bare-token answer so exact matching is not punitive. Stated uncertainty is candid and largely matches the claim, including the disclosure that the scanner advances three residues after a hit and would therefore miss overlapping sequons. That disclosure, however, is a known deviation from the claim's 'reports each hit' wording that the case set does not probe, so the uncertainty section acknowledges a gap rather than closing it.",
    "No stronger grade was passed over; A is the top grade and was the proposal. The stronger_grade_considered reasoning is sound on oracle provenance and scoring mechanics but treats A as a function of oracle quality and case count alone, without testing coverage against the claim's stated scope, which is where this design falls short of A.",
    "prior_objections is empty, so this criterion does not apply; no earlier concern is answered or left unresolved."
  ],
  "objections": [
    "Scope mismatch: claim scope is 'single-letter amino-acid protein sequences supplied directly to the skill', but scanner cases cover exactly one sequence (P01588) and only its three positive hits. The candidate's own candidate_scope concedes non-transferability, which is an admission that the evidence is narrower than the claim it grades.",
    "The 'X is not proline' clause of expected_behavior is never exercised against the scanner. P01588 contains no N-P-[S/T] triplet, so a scanner that ignored the proline rule entirely would pass all five cases.",
    "The skill is known (per the candidate's own uncertainty note) to advance three residues after a hit, which contradicts 'reports each hit' for overlapping sequons such as N-N-T-T. No case contains an overlap, so a known implementation deviation from the claim remains untested.",
    "Case epo_sequon_1's prompt partially leaks its own answer: it supplies the format \"Asn-X-...\" so the only unknown token is 'Ser/Thr'. This materially reduces that case's discriminative power.",
    "All three positional cases query an ordinal (FIRST/SECOND/THIRD) rather than asking for the complete hit list, so the scanner's enumeration completeness and its handling of the terminal window are inferred rather than observed."
  ],
  "required_revisions": [
    "Add at least one scanner case on a sequence containing an N-P-[S/T] triplet that must be rejected, with the expected answer fixed independently (e.g. a second curated UniProt entry whose annotated N-linked sites exclude a proline-containing triplet, with the same motif/annotation coincidence verified in-case).",
    "Add a scanner case containing overlapping sequons (e.g. ...N-N-T-T...) with the full expected hit list, so the skip-by-three behavior is either confirmed absent or recorded as a failure rather than left untested.",
    "Add at least one additional protein sequence, including a negative control sequence with zero canonical sequons, so the claim's arbitrary-sequence scope is represented by more than a single 193-mer.",
    "Convert at least one positional case to request the complete comma-separated hit list rather than an ordinal, so enumeration completeness is directly scored.",
    "Reword the definitional case so the expected token is not embedded in the prompt, or drop it from the count of cases credited toward the behavioral claim."
  ]
}
```
